blocks.text: Frequency Encoding replaced each category with its proportion of the overall dataset, a genuinely bounded number between 0 and 1. Count encoding uses the exact same underlying idea, but skips the normalization step, replacing each category with its raw count instead, a genuinely small change in the formula that carries real, practical consequences worth understanding clearly.

This topic covers exactly how count encoding differs mechanically from frequency encoding, why raw counts genuinely become sensitive to dataset size in a way proportions are not, why count encoded features often genuinely need the scaling techniques from the previous module afterward, the same collision risk carried over from the previous topic, and the specific, real cases where using a raw count actually makes more genuine sense than a normalized proportion.
1. The One Genuine Mechanical Difference

blocks.alt: Frequency encoding gives a rate while count encoding gives a raw number

blocks.text: Frequency encoding takes a genuine category count and divides it by the total number of rows, producing a bounded proportion. Count encoding stops one step earlier, using that genuine raw count directly, with no division at all. A category appearing 150 times becomes 0.15 under frequency encoding, but genuinely stays 150 under count encoding.

This is genuinely the entire mechanical difference between these two topics, everything else, the collision risk, the leakage discipline, the lack of target usage, carries over identically from the previous topic, only this one specific computation step actually changes.
2. Why Raw Counts Are Genuinely Sensitive to Dataset Size

blocks.alt: A small dataset produces small counts while a large dataset produces large counts

blocks.text: A genuine count of 100 means something very different depending on how large the overall dataset actually is, in a dataset with 10000 rows, a count of 100 genuinely represents a fairly rare category, just 1 percent of the data. In a dataset with only 100 rows, that genuine same count of 100 would mean every single row belongs to that one category.

This is a genuinely real, practical fragility that frequency encoding proportion based approach avoids entirely, a frequency of 0.01 genuinely means the same thing, rare, regardless of whether the underlying dataset has 100 rows or 10 million, while a raw count of 100 genuinely does not carry that same portable, comparable meaning.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Raw counts are genuinely not comparable across datasets of different sizes, while proportions genuinely are. This matters directly if training and test data ever come from meaningfully different sized samples.

blocks.text: 3. A Worked Example
Computing both count and frequency encoding on the same city column, side by side, makes their genuine difference directly concrete.

code.content:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "city": ["mumbai", "delhi", "mumbai", "bangalore", "mumbai", "delhi"],
})

count_map = df["city"].value_counts()
freq_map = df["city"].value_counts(normalize=True)

df["city_count"] = df["city"].map(count_map)
df["city_freq"] = df["city"].map(freq_map)

print(df)

blocks.text: mumbai genuinely becomes 3 under count encoding and 0.5 under frequency encoding, both genuinely derived from the exact same underlying category counts, differing only by that one normalization step covered above.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: When unsure which to use, compute both count and frequency encoding side by side, exactly as in this worked example, and check which one correlates more strongly with the target before committing to either.

blocks.text: 4. Why Count Encoded Features Often Need Scaling

blocks.alt: A raw count often needs scaling before use

blocks.text: Because raw counts are genuinely unbounded, ranging from 1 up to however many rows a genuinely popular category might have, count encoded features often carry a genuinely wide, unpredictable scale, unlike the neat 0 to 1 range frequency encoding naturally provides. This directly connects back to the entire previous module, a count encoded feature is frequently a genuine, good candidate for standardization or another scaling technique afterward, exactly the kind of preparation covered in real depth in Feature Scaling.

This is a genuinely practical, real consideration worth planning for from the start, count encoding does not, on its own, produce a feature ready to sit alongside other, already scaled features without some further genuine preparation.

blocks.text: 5. The Same Collision Risk, Carried Forward

blocks.alt: Two categories with the same count collide just like with frequency encoding

blocks.text: Exactly as with frequency encoding, if two genuinely different categories happen to appear the same number of times, category X and category Y both appearing exactly 40 times, for instance, they both genuinely receive the identical count, 40, and a model can no longer genuinely distinguish between them. Switching from a proportion to a raw count does nothing to fix this specific, real limitation, it carries over unchanged from the previous topic.

This is worth stating directly, count encoding is not genuinely a fix for anything frequency encoding got wrong, it is a deliberate, different choice with its own tradeoffs, sharing this exact same real risk in common with its sibling technique.
6. When Raw Count Genuinely Makes More Sense

blocks.alt: When absolute volume matters, count encoding is the right choice

blocks.text: Some genuine real cases specifically call for a raw magnitude rather than a normalized proportion, the number of reviews a product genuinely has is often meaningful precisely as a raw count, a product with 5000 reviews genuinely conveys a different, real signal than a product with 50, in a way that is not simply about proportion of a whole dataset.

A genuine popularity or activity count works similarly, the raw number itself often aligns directly with real world intuition in a way a normalized 0 to 1 proportion would obscure, exactly the kind of case where count encoding raw magnitude is genuinely the more natural, appropriate choice over frequency encoding.

blocks.text: 7. Count Encoding Versus Frequency Encoding, Summarized

blocks.alt: Count gives a raw number while frequency gives a normalized rate

blocks.text: Both techniques genuinely derive from the exact same underlying category counts, differing only in whether that count is normalized into a proportion. Frequency encoding genuine bounded range makes it more portable and comparable across differently sized datasets, while count encoding genuine raw magnitude can carry more direct, intuitive meaning in specific real contexts like popularity or activity counts.

Neither is genuinely, universally the better choice, the decision comes down to whether the real, raw magnitude itself matters for the specific problem at hand, or whether a portable, comparable proportion is genuinely the safer, more general default.
8. Count Encoding Versus What Comes Next

blocks.alt: Count encoding is covered here, target encoding comes next

blocks.text: Frequency Encoding and Count Encoding together cover the genuine family of techniques that derive a meaningful number directly from a category own presence in the data, without ever consulting the target column at all. The remaining topics in this module take a genuinely different, more powerful, but also genuinely riskier approach.

The next topic, Target Encoding, introduces exactly that shift, replacing a category with a statistic derived from the actual target variable itself, a genuinely more powerful signal, but one that reopens the exact leakage concerns first covered back in the Data Leakage topic, in a new, specific form.
